subtype: Approach: expects things to work because they should [Pitfall]
passage:
Ritwik had worked hard for three years: top marks in the lab, a project he was proud of, late nights before every submission. So when the company interview was fixed for Thursday morning, he did not open a single page about the company. Hard work always paid off, he told his roommate, so the interview would go well.
The train was delayed, and he walked in breathless with ten minutes to spare.
"What do you know about our product line?" the panel asked. Then: "How would you approach this case study?" He knew neither. He answered with stories about effort, and the panel nodded politely and wrote very little.

qa.q: Which day was the interview fixed for?
qa.a: The interview was fixed for Thursday morning.

qa.q: What did Ritwik expect about the interview, and why?
qa.a: Ritwik expected it to go well because hard work always paid off, and felt confident enough to skip any preparation.

qa.q: What could Ritwik have done in the days before the interview?
qa.a: Ritwik could have read about the company and practised a sample case study, since the panel asked about those exact things and general effort could not answer them.

qa.q: How might the panel see Ritwik's answers?
qa.a: The panel nodded politely and wrote very little, so they may have seen a hard-working person who had not prepared for their questions.

grounding: A student assumes that working hard in general means the interview will go well and does no preparation.
